risks.note: Tea is an agricultural product wholly dependent on weather; global climatic change has made conditions erratic and unpredictable, and extreme weather impacts both crop and quality. El Nino-induced weather extremes continue to hit crop yields despite afforestation, irrigation and flood-control mitigation, and BRSR identifies Climate Change as a material risk with negative financial implications. During the year, low rainfall and inclement weather cut production at the Nagrijuli, Kharikatia and Dhoedaam estates, and inadequate, delayed rainfall in Upper Assam and the North Bank produced poor cropping from January to March 2026.
risks.risk: Climate and weather dependence of an agricultural crop

risks.note: Climate change is bringing new pests and diseases, incidence has increased and some pests have become resistant to existing pesticides. With chemical options constrained by residue limits, the Company relies on bio formulations, whose effectiveness falls in extreme weather and whose availability in the required quantity and quality in the local market remains a challenge - the reason it has started its own production unit at Romai Tea Estate.
risks.risk: Pest and disease pressure with shrinking chemical options

risks.note: Strict international MRL standards and certifications add complexity to exports. The EU's stricter Maximum Residue Limits for neonicotinoids, and inconsistent chemical usage among small growers, threaten export viability and domestic production; the evolving EU-2026 MRL requirements are expected to increase compliance challenges globally, and remaining compliant with the new 2026 MRL regime is named as a specific challenge for UK/Europe exports. Strict EU MRL rules are cited as threatening some 40M kg of Indian exports, with costly compliance testing.
risks.risk: Regulatory / MRL compliance risk in export markets

risks.note: Ongoing wars (Russia-Ukraine, West Asia), India-Pakistan tensions and global inflation have led to weaker demand, volatile pricing and increased shipping costs. Input costs for fuel, gas, fertilizers, packaging materials and food have risen sharply following the conflicts in West Asia and the near three-month closure of the Strait of Hormuz, while Red Sea shipping is yet to normalise and freight and insurance costs have risen significantly.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and macroeconomic disruption to trade and input costs

risks.note: Rising imports of lower-cost teas from Kenya, Nepal and other producing countries pressure domestic pricing and export competitiveness; lower prevailing Kenyan prices are encouraging overseas buyers to shift part of their sourcing to that market, and a price imbalance between Indian and African CTC teas, alongside sluggish global trade, continues to affect competitiveness.
risks.risk: Import competition and export price competitiveness

risks.note: Domestic tea prices are largely driven by supply-demand dynamics and periods of over-production can result in lower market realisations. CTC demand remained subdued on weaker demand from domestic buyers including large packeteers; the CTC market was subdued from April to November 2025 with prices declining significantly in August and September 2025, and prices in both CTC and Orthodox categories were lower than the previous year.
risks.risk: Tea price cyclicality and demand softness, particularly in CTC

risks.note: Management identifies reining in escalating costs, particularly wages and fuel, as the biggest challenge alongside protecting the crop; a staff salary increase took effect from 1st April 2025 and was absorbed only through higher production and product mix.
risks.risk: Cost inflation, especially wages and fuel

risks.note: BRSR identifies Occupational Health & Safety as a material risk with negative financial implications: tea cultivation and processing expose workers to manual labour, machinery and agrochemical use, mitigated through regular safety audits and drills, awareness sessions on safe handling of equipment and chemicals, PPE distribution and strict adherence to OHS protocols.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety on estates
